title: Bread and wine (Genesis 14:17–20)
hookLine: Melchisedech, king and priest, brings out bread and wine; named in the Roman Canon
last: GO, AND I WILL SHOW YOU.

lines: A KING COMES OUT TO MEET HIM.
cards: Some characters in the Bible get whole books. This one gets three verses, and then vanishes.

Abram has just come back from a night raid: four kings had carried off his nephew Lot, and Abram chased them north with three hundred eighteen men and brought everyone home. On the road back, a king comes out to meet him.
Not with an army. Not with a bill. With bread, and wine.
Then he's gone from the story, and yet his name is still spoken in a prayer at Catholic altars.

teach.h: A KING AND A PRIEST AT ONCE.
teach.b: First, who he is. In the Douay-Rheims: "But Melchisedech the king of Salem, bringing forth bread and wine, for he was the priest of the most high God." A king and a priest at once.
His name in Hebrew means king of righteousness. Salem means peace, and later tradition identifies it with Jerusalem. He has no family tree, no beginning or end in the story.
He just appears. Second, what he does. He blesses Abram by the most high God, maker of heaven and earth, and blesses God for the victory.

teach.h: ABRAM IS BLESSED AND GIVES A TENTH.
teach.b: And Abram gives him a tenth of everything. The man God called to be a blessing is himself blessed by a stranger. Third, where he turns up again.

teach.h: A PRIEST FOREVER, IN THE PSALM.
teach.b: In a psalm, God says to the king, in the Douay-Rheims: "Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech."
The Letter to the Hebrews applies that line to Christ: a priest not by birth in Aaron's family, but like Melchisedech, forever. Fourth, why Catholics say his name.

In the Roman Canon, the first Eucharistic Prayer of the Mass, the priest asks God to accept the offering as he once accepted the gifts of Abel, the sacrifice of Abraham, and the offering of the high priest Melchisedech.
The Catechism sees in his bread and wine a sign that points ahead to the Eucharist.
Readers in other churches, following Hebrews, also see in him a picture of Christ's priesthood, and draw the link to the altar differently or not at all.
Either way, the shape is the same: a priest, a blessing, bread and wine, long ago.

how: In the Roman Canon, the priest asks God to accept the Mass's offering as he accepted the offering of Melchisedech, and Genesis 14:18–20 is read on the solemnity of the Body and Blood of Christ in one year of the cycle.

o: one of the four kings who carried off Lot
the priest-king who brought Abram bread and wine
a prophet who anointed Abram as a king

games.q: what's inside the meeting — tap the pairs.

s: Melchisedech appears in only a few verses of Genesis
three verses, then he's gone. yet a psalm, Hebrews and the Mass all remember him.
Melchisedech is a priest from Aaron's family
he comes long before Aaron. Hebrews contrasts the two.
Melchisedech blesses Abram, and Abram gives him a tenth of everything.

games.q: you're a king and a priest. Abram is on the road home from rescuing Lot, tired and dusty. how do you meet him?
o: with an army, to claim a share of the spoils.
with bread and wine, and a blessing.
with a demand that he pay tribute.
games.why: Melchisedech brings forth bread and wine and blesses Abram by the most high God. Abram gives him a tenth.

practice: Put any bread or food in front of you, or picture a loaf on a table, and think how much it took to get here: wheat in a field, rain, hands at harvest, an oven, a truck; grapes on a vine, crushed and waited on.
If you pray, give thanks for the food and for the people who brought it to you.

wordCard.voice: Melchisedech, the king and priest who brought out bread and wine to bless Abram, a sign Catholics see of the Eucharist. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Melchizedek, king of righteousness. Douay-Rheims spells it Melchisedech.

carryVoice: Your line: bread and wine, long ago. Three verses, and still named at the altar. Day three hundred forty-six, done.
